t: A low-cost 3D-printed robot arm pair for teaching robots by example.
steps: Choose your path. Download the free STL files from The Robot Studio on GitHub and print the parts, or buy a kit from a shop such as Seeed Studio or WowRobo.
Order the servos, bus servo adapter boards, and power supplies from the parts list. Many kits include all of these.
Install Python and the free LeRobot library from Hugging Face on your computer.
Plug in one servo at a time and run the lerobot-setup-motors command to give each one its ID.
Assemble both arms by following the official SO-101 guide from Hugging Face.
Calibrate the leader and the follower with the guide's calibration steps.
Try the teleoperation example. Move the leader arm and watch the follower copy you.
Record a few demos and train your first policy with LeRobot.
meta: Wild Open. From $199. A few stores.
